title: The Defeat of the Dragon
definition: The doctrine of The Defeat of the Dragon teaches that revelation shows Satan as the dragon who opposes God’s people and is finally defeated by God’s power and the victory of the Lamb.
summary: The Defeat of the Dragon names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. Revelation shows Satan as the dragon who opposes God’s people and is finally defeated by God’s power and the victory of the Lamb. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to The Defeat of the Dragon because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: Revelation shows Satan as the dragon who opposes God’s people and is finally defeated by God’s power and the victory of the Lamb. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because the church may feel surrounded if it forgets that the dragon’s rage is temporary and doomed. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Overcome by the blood of the Lamb and faithful testimony. Do not love your comfort more than Christ when pressure comes. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
